title: Interstate banking deregulation on credit supply

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
The research question lends itself to a Difference-in-Differences (DID) analysis, as we are dealing with a treatment (interstate banking deregulation) that varies across states over time. The key assumption for DID is the parallel trends assumption, which states that the trend in the outcome variable (log loans-to-assets ratio) for the treatment group would have been the same as the trend for the control group in the absence of the treatment.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Load necessary libraries
library(readr)
library(plm)
library(lmtest)
library(car)

# Read the data from the CSV file
data <- read_csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s05_data.csv")

# Convert the data to a panel data frame
p pdata <- pdata.frame(data, index = c("unit_id", "period"))

# Run the DID analysis using a fixed effects model
model_did <- plm(y ~ treated * post + post + treated, data = pdata, 
                 index = c("unit_id", "period"), model = "fixed")

# Print the results
summary(model_did)

# Perform a robustness check: test for parallel trends
pre_treatment_periods <- pdata[pdata$period < 4, ]
model_pre_did <- plm(y ~ treated * post + post + treated, data = pre_treatment_periods, 
                      index = c("unit_id", "period"), model = "fixed")

# Print the results
summary(model_pre_did)

# Another robustness check: test for common trends in all pre-treatment periods
for (i in 1:3) {
  pre_period_data <- pdata[pdata$period == i, ]
  model_common_trend <- lm(y ~ treated, data = pre_period_data)
  print(paste("Period:", i, " Common trend test:", coef(model_common_trend)[2]))
}
```

## 3. Expected Findings
We expect the coefficient on the interaction term `treated * post` to be positive, indicating that interstate banking deregulation increased credit supply in deregulated states compared to regulated states. The magnitude of this effect will depend on the specifics of the data, but we anticipate that the deregulation will lead to an increase in the log loans-to-assets ratio of around 5-10%. This increase reflects the expected expansion in lending activity following deregulation, as banks are able to operate more freely across state lines. The exact magnitude will depend on various factors, including the level of competition among banks, the demand for loans, and the overall economic conditions in the states.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: DID — treated=deregulated states, control=still-regulated; shock=deregulation date
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Credit supply increases significantly after deregulation
